acme_ops: hey team — since we flipped the reserved freeze for rdw-embed-lite-v4 we're seeing inconsistent embedding lengths from /v1/embeddings. some requests return 1536, some 1024. mostly when batch_size > 1, started ~07:00 UTC, ~10% failure rate.

ali_support: thanks for reporting — can you paste a minimal curl and an example response? also confirm the exact model id + pinned variant you're calling.

acme_ops: sure — calling rdw-embed-lite-v4 with the reserved freeze tag. sample curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rdw-embed-lite-v4@frozen-20260310","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3","doc4","doc5","doc6","doc7","doc8"]}'
```

response (truncated):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[... 1536 floats ...]}, {"embedding":[... 1536 floats ...]}, {"embedding":[... 1024 floats ...]}, ...]}
```

acme_ops: we tried explicitly setting variant=rdw-embed-lite-v4@frozen-20260310 and still saw the flip. headers from one response: `x-rdw-variant: rdw-embed-lite-v4@frozen-20260310`, `x-rdw-serving: reserved-pool-5`, `x-rdw-model-hash: abc123`.

maria_ml: pinging ML & runtime for triage — this pattern (mixed dims within a single batch) smells like routing hitting two different artifacts (e.g., a legacy non-updated tokenizer/embedding head on one artifact). do you have request ids? any correlation with specific items in the batch?

acme_ops: Request-IDs: req-9a2, req-9a3, req-9a4 (attached). It looks like item index 3 in the batch is the one that flips most frequently. It isn't content-dependent as we tried identical inputs.

jason_sre: can you confirm batch size and whether you're using client-side retry or parallel workers? also any logs from the ingest/indexer side?

acme_ops: batch_size=8, single-threaded call (no client retry). downstream indexer fails on 1024-length vectors with schema validation errors. we've had to throttle ingestion.

ali_support: thanks — giving this to runtime + routing. I'll attempt a repro in staging with identical params.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rdw-routing-fix/2026-03-12 -> canary (reserved-pool routing tweak).

maria_ml: quick update from local repro: when the routing decision falls back to an older quantized artifact (quant-8 variant) we see 1024 dims; the main float artifact produces 1536. root cause appears to be alias resolution for the frozen variant pointing at two artifacts during the reserved freeze transition. batchpad/continuous-batching can cause a single batch to be split across serving workers, exposing the mismatch. repro steps I used: 1) send 2 concurrent batch requests with identical payloads; 2) observe variant header; 3) compare embedding lengths.

ali_support: short mitigation: call with explicit model_version param (e.g., `model_version=rdw-embed-lite-v4@build-20260310`) which forces artifact id and avoids alias resolution. not ideal long-term but should stop flips immediately. also try batch_size=1 while we fix routing.

jason_sre: we can temporarily enforce pinned-variant routing on reserved-pool-5 to prevent alias fallback. rolling that now to canary, ETA ~2h to full.

acme_ops: that's good. any guidance on re-ingesting items that failed? we had ~12k vectors rejected.

ali_support: please hold off re-ingest until I confirm routing enforcement completed. after fix, reprocess those messages — they should index normally. we'll also provide a script to detect mixed-dim responses for safety.

maria_ml: long-term fix: add a rollout-time validation that verifies embed dimension parity across all artifacts behind an alias, and fail alias update if parity differs. adding to model onboarding checklist + gating in the compilation/alias service.

acme_ops: appreciated. can you share timelines and a follow-up postmortem? downstream ops need it for the incident report.

ali_support: will send incident note + timeline after we finish the routing enforcement and confirm re-ingest results. provisional ETA 2 hours for mitigation, 48 hours for postmortem and permanent guard.

acme_ops: :thumbsup: thanks for the quick response — holding for your go-ahead before reprocessing.

jason_sre: routing enforcement rolled to canary, monitoring for mixed-dim traces. will update here.

maria_ml: added a probe to evals that will run a dimensional parity check on canary traffic and alert if mismatch > 0.1%.

ali_support: marking this thread as blocked -> routing enforcement in progress. we'll follow up when mitigation is live.

acme_ops: thanks everyone — fingers crossed.
